rationale:
ROUND 2. The code is UNCHANGED from round 1: the gating objection asked for reuse-search EVIDENCE, not a different fix, and churning code to answer an evidence objection would be the wrong response. Both objections are answered below with the checks actually run.

ANSWER TO reuse_agent, edit 6 (HIGH — 'does council 18fe4035 / migration 243's reader-side fix already add a freshness/staleness signal that mixedCommitNote duplicates or conflicts with?'). The seat is right that the landmines point straight at it and round 1's grounded_in never engaged. Checked, four ways, and the answer is COMPLEMENTARY, not duplicate:
(a) WHAT 18fe4035 ACTUALLY FIXED on the reader side is enumerated by its own trail note (doc_notes, subject_key diagnose_code_lookup, 2026-07-27 'later the same day'): kind=content now searches COALESCE(body,'') OR content; each hit is marked [body] or [decl]; the excerpt is taken AROUND the match; an empty result became an ANSWER ('answered: 0 rows — searched 4,535 indexed symbols'); and the migration-243-to-roll degrade window is named. That is BODY COVERAGE. The note does not mention commit identity, commit_sha, or staleness once.
(b) THE FRESHNESS HALF IS A DIFFERENT PIECE OF WORK — bugs_open/059 plus 108 defect A, commit 87d0bcf97, council b5285973, migration 250 — and its verdict is BY CONSTRUCTION a single high-water mark: freshnessBanner reads one row (ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1) and renders 'it describes commit %s'. A single-row read cannot express 'and 400 other rows describe an older one', so mixedCommitNote is not a second opinion on the same question; it answers a question that mechanism structurally cannot ask.
(c) NOTHING IN THE TREE REPORTS COMMIT HETEROGENEITY. `grep -rn 'DISTINCT commit_sha\|DISTINCT COALESCE(commit_sha' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/` returns exactly ONE line, and it is the line this plan adds. So there is no existing helper to reuse and nothing to conflict with.
(d) IT WAS NEITHER ADDRESSED NOR DEFERRED — it was never considered. `grep -rni 'spans.*commit|multiple commit|mixed commit|two commit_sha'` over architecture_review/, migrations 243 and 244, and bugs_closed/108 returns ZERO hits. The 07-27 note is explicit about what it left owed (council-gate has no code_lookup step; markdown is unreachable pending the kind CHECK relaxation) and a mixed-commit index is not on that list.
AND THE POSITIVE REUSE POINT the seat should weigh: this plan does not add a sibling note-renderer. It extends codeIndexScope — the helper 18fe4035 CREATED — and preserves the exact property that note insists on in its own words, 'used by BOTH lanes that answer code checks ... One judgement, not a sibling copy that drifts (016b section 9)': the distinct-commit count rides the COUNT query that helper already runs (no extra round trip), and both readers (diagnose_code_lookup, diagnose_load_runtime) are wired in this same commit.

ANSWER TO reuse_agent, edit 4 (low — 'no evidence an existing confirmed-vs-stored / reconciliation-cohort helper was searched for'). It was searched for; round 1 just did not show the searches. `grep -rn 'prune_floor|floor_ratio|reconcil' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/` returns no guard of this shape — every 'reconcil' hit is either reconcile_superseded_reviews (a standalone review-status sweep, no delete floor) or prose in comments. `grep -rn 'DELETE FROM' --include=*.go` over platform/ internal/ pkg/ services/ returns 15 statements, of which exactly four are delete-what-this-run-did-not-see; none has any completeness check. The nearest EXISTING relative is LOCK-007's lockedAssetKeys (asset_lock_guard.go) — a shared guard answering 'may automation overwrite this?' for WRITERS, which this deliberately mirrors in shape (derive the guard predicate from the operation's own predicate; fail closed) without sharing code, because a lock set and a count ratio have nothing in common but the discipline. Recorded as the relation in CTXA-025.

ANSWER TO editquality's two low objections (it approved). (1) 'Fail-closed on cErr treats a transient lock timeout the same as a genuine partial run.' Yes, deliberately, and the asymmetry of cost is the whole argument: a false refusal retains stale rows for one cycle and the NEXT healthy run prunes them (the delete is defined against the current commit, not against this run), whereas a false permit is the index. The reason is distinguishable where it matters — prune_status='refused_unmeasurable' is a different value from 'refused_floor' and the error text rides the note. (2) 'The 24h doc_notes suppression window is hardcoded.' Deliberate: one more knob on a surface with NO automated consumer, and the per-occurrence record is kept by the log regardless — the note is the digest, not the event stream. Both are stated in the code comments rather than left to be inferred.

THE ORIGINAL RATIONALE, unchanged: bugs_open/135. IndexCodeSymbolsAction ends every run with an UNCONDITIONAL reconciliation delete — DELETE FROM code_symbols WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2 — so everything this run did not re-upsert is destroyed. That is correct when the run saw the whole repo and catastrophic when it did not, and NOTHING checks that it did. A partial or truncated tarball fetch, a moved directory, a permissions change on the extracted tree, or an analyser failure that yields a short Output all produce a small-but-nonzero result with NO error: the run upserts what little it saw and deletes the rest. The index is not corrupted, it is emptied of everything the bad run missed, and the read side then answers zero rows confidently. bugs_closed/108's fix deliberately made that empty answer more confidently worded ('the query was RUN and matched none'), so a silently-thinned index now lies harder than before that fix. It is currently invisible: the prune is conditional on nothing so there is no branch to log, `pruned: 4000` is reported as a SUCCESS counter (the number that should be the alarm, presented as output), and orchestration_states retains ~2 days so the evidence ages out before anyone correlates it with a suddenly-thin index. Measured live 2026-07-31: 4,992 rows, one repo (gqls/agentchassis), five kinds, all at one commit — so the guard is being armed while the index is healthy and today's prune ratios are ~1.0. The design here is the END of an argument, not the start of one: this defect arrived as a bug_historian objection inside an unrelated markdown-indexing plan (corr 7ba5b8c4), was fixed inside that plan, drew three further rounds of objections about its own machinery, and was then SPLIT OUT deliberately because it is pre-existing and independent of that plan. Candidates 1-3 of the case file are what those six rounds produced. Two things are deliberately generalised beyond the one call site, and one thing is deliberately NOT: (a) the decision RULE lives in its own file as pure functions of counts, because three other live call sites share the identical destructive shape (populate_nav_tables_action.go:147, site_db_actions.go:1474, save_page_sections_action.go:532) and the next thread to touch one should not re-derive this argument; (b) the read side is told when the index no longer describes a single commit, because a REFUSED prune retains stale rows by design and the existing freshness banner reads one row (ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1) and would announce the newest commit for a part-stale corpus — trading a loud catastrophe for a quiet lie is not a fix. (c) The three other call sites are NOT converted here: each is another lane's live territory and each needs its own cohorts measured rather than assumed; they are named in the new file instead. CONSUMERS TOLD (RFC 002 ruling 3): the only consumer of index_code_symbols' result is the code-indexer workflow's complete step (result_from: index_result), which is unaffected — every existing key keeps its meaning and new keys are added beside them; the consumers of the read-side helper are diagnose_code_lookup and diagnose_load_runtime, and BOTH are changed here in the same commit rather than left to diverge. No config anywhere sets prune_floor_ratio, so the guard arms at its code default of 0.5 on the next roll — that is stated, not hidden.
submitter: bugfix 11 session (bugs_open/135, prune floor) — ROUND 2, answering reuse_agent HIGH on edit 6 and low on edit 4

plan.summary: A reconciliation prune that deletes everything a run did not re-write must first show that the run saw the corpus. Adds a shared, resolvable FLOOR: per symbol kind AND across the repo's distinct file paths, this run must have re-confirmed at least prune_floor_ratio (default 0.5, 0 disables) of what is stored, or the prune is refused whole, recorded durably in doc_notes, and reported in the action result beside the run's input size. Fails CLOSED when the floor cannot be measured. The read side gains one note so a retained-stale index can no longer be described as being at one commit.

edits.rationale: The decision rule, as pure functions of counts, with no SQL and no knowledge of any one table — because the measurement is per-table and the rule is not. COHORTS rather than one total: a run that re-confirms 95% of rows can still have lost 100% of one class, and a single whole-corpus ratio hides that completely. The floor is RESOLVABLE (step config, 0 disables) and the refusal text names that remedy, because a large legitimate deletion is a real event and a guard with no exit is a defect in a guard's costume (guardian seat, round 5 of the 7ba5b8c4 trail). Also placed here, in comments, are the three other live call sites of the same destructive shape, so the next thread to touch one starts from the end of this argument.

The case file's own verification rule is verify-the-failing-branch: 'a green run over a healthy repo proves only that the guard is inert.' Splitting the rule from the SQL is what makes every branch reachable without a DB. The wiped-kind case asserts its own premise first (whole-corpus ratio 0.99) so it cannot silently stop testing what it is named for.
edits.sketch:
TestEvaluatePruneFloorAllowsAHealthyRun            — 3048/3050 etc, allowed, Detail() still populated
TestEvaluatePruneFloorRefusesATruncatedRun        — 38% confirmed: refused, and the text carries REFUSED, '1160 of 3048', 'NOTHING was deleted', 'prune_floor_ratio', '0 disables'
TestEvaluatePruneFloorRefusesAWipedKindThatTheTotalWouldHide — 4930/4963 = 99% overall, kind=interface 0/33: asserts the 99% premise, then asserts refusal. This is why cohorts exist.
TestEvaluatePruneFloorNewCohortCannotRefuse       — Stored 0 must not refuse
TestEvaluatePruneFloorDisabledIsAllowedAndSaysSo  — 0 permits the delete AND says DISABLED/unchecked
TestEvaluatePruneFloorNegativeDisablesAndFlagsClamped
TestEvaluatePruneFloorAboveOneIsClampedNotUnsatisfiable
TestEvaluatePruneFloorBoundaryIsInclusive         — 50/100 at floor 0.5 passes; 49/100 refuses
TestEvaluatePruneFloorNoCohortsAllows             — first-ever run must bootstrap
TestPruneFloorCohortListCaps, TestPruneFloorFromConfig (9 shapes incl. garbage -> default, not 0)

edits.rationale: The prune must now earn the right to run. FAILS CLOSED on an unmeasurable floor: the measurement is the only thing between a partial run and a deleted index, and retaining stale rows costs a later prune that the next healthy run performs anyway — a refused prune is self-healing (the delete is defined against the CURRENT commit, not against this run), a wrong delete is not. That self-healing property is also why the refusal is all-or-nothing rather than per-kind: a partial prune is harder to reason about and avoids almost nothing.

The measurement, in the two units that fail independently: one cohort per symbol KIND (a 95% whole-repo ratio can hide one wiped kind — and this is also what protects a kind this code has never heard of, since a Go-only run cannot delete a future markdown corpus whose cohort reads 0% confirmed), plus one cohort in DISTINCT PATHS (rows measure how much this run WROTE; paths measure how much of the repo it SAW, which is the property that actually fails on a truncated tarball). Both halves use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2, the exact complement of the DELETE's own IS DISTINCT FROM $2, so the guard can never end up measuring a different population from the one at risk.
edits.sketch:
SELECT COALESCE(kind,'(none)'),
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE commit_sha IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2) AS confirmed,
       count(*)                                                   AS stored
FROM code_symbols WHERE repo = $1 GROUP BY 1

SELECT count(DISTINCT path) FILTER (WHERE commit_sha IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2),
       count(DISTINCT path)
FROM code_symbols WHERE repo = $1

-- measured AFTER the run's upserts and immediately before the DELETE, so a
-- symbol whose upsert FAILED counts as unconfirmed — which is exactly the
-- partial-run signal the guard is for.

edits.rationale: Candidate 2: a refusal that lives only in logger.Error is the 034/076 shape ('no error anywhere' usually means no error surface), and orchestration_states retains ~2 days. doc_notes and NOT site_work_items — the failed attempt inside the originating plan: site_work_items.site_id/handler_agent/pipeline are all NOT NULL and this indexer is repo-wide with no site. subject_type='action' + subject_key='index_code_symbols' is where this subsystem's trail already lives (2 rows, verified 2026-07-31). Reuses insertDocNote rather than adding a second INSERT. Says plainly in its own doc comment that there is NO automated consumer, rather than implying a triage lifecycle that does not exist.

The hazard this fix INTRODUCES, closed in the same commit. A refused prune retains stale rows on purpose, and the freshness banner reads exactly one row (ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1) — after a refusal the newest row is this run's, so the banner announces the new commit for a corpus that is only partly at it. That is bugs_closed/108's lie one layer along. The count rides on the COUNT query loadCodeIndexScope already runs (no extra round trip), and the note is EMPTY in the healthy single-commit case because a banner that always fires stops being read. Note the state was already reachable before this change, via the pre-existing 'no commit_sha, prune skipped' branch.

The SECOND reader of the same helper. This lane's verdict prompt is cite-or-abstain and therefore ACTS on absence, so it needs the qualifier at least as much as the council's lane does. Changed in the same commit rather than left to diverge — one judgement, not a sibling copy (016b §9).

Asserts the note's SILENCE in the healthy case as strictly as its noise in the mixed one — a note that always fires is a note nobody reads — and that a failed scope read does not assert a commit spread it never measured.

grounded_in: ROUND 2 — the reuse check, (a): doc_notes subject_key='diagnose_code_lookup', 2026-07-27 'later the same day' (D11 layer 1, council 18fe4035, migration 243), enumerating what its reader-side fix consisted of: "kind=content searches (COALESCE(body,'') ILIKE ... OR content ILIKE ...) — body OR declaration ... Each hit is marked [body] or [decl] ... The excerpt is taken AROUND the match ... AN EMPTY RESULT IS NOW AN ANSWER. 'answered: 0 rows — searched 4,535 indexed symbols' ... THE DEGRADE IS NAMED, NOT SILENT." No mention of commit identity or staleness anywhere in the note.

ROUND 2 — the reuse check, (a) continued: that same note's own list of what it left OWED is explicit and does not include a mixed-commit index: "STILL NOT FIXED HERE: council-gate has no code_lookup step at all ... Also still unreachable: markdown. 0 of 4,535 index rows are markdown ... that needs the kind CHECK constraint relaxed, which is its own migration."

ROUND 2 — the reuse check, (b): the freshness mechanism is a DIFFERENT lineage and is structurally single-row. diagnose_code_lookup_action.go: `SELECT COALESCE(commit_sha,''), COALESCE(ref,''), commit_time, updated_at FROM code_symbols WHERE ($1 = '' OR repo = $1) ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1`, rendering 'it describes commit %s%s'. Its own comment names its provenance: 'The verdict is a function of the indexed COMMIT, not of updated_at (bugs_open/108 defect A ...)' — i.e. migration 250 / commit 87d0bcf97, not 243.

ROUND 2 — the reuse check, (c): `grep -rn 'DISTINCT commit_sha\|DISTINCT COALESCE(commit_sha' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/` returns exactly one line — `diagnose_code_lookup_action.go:210`, the line this plan adds. Nothing else in the tree measures commit spread, so there is no prior helper to reuse and nothing to conflict with.

ROUND 2 — the reuse check, (d): `grep -rni 'spans.*commit|multiple commit|mixed commit|two commit_sha'` over docs024/architecture_review/, sql_for_agents/243*, sql_for_agents/244*, bugs_closed/108* returns ZERO hits. Neither addressed nor explicitly deferred by the prior council decision: not considered.

ROUND 2 — the positive reuse property, from the 07-27 note this plan is accused of not consulting: 'codeIndexScope carries it, is read once per action run, and is used by BOTH lanes that answer code checks — diagnose_code_lookup (the council's verify tier) and diagnose_load_runtime (the diagnosis lane, whose verdicter's cite-or-abstain acts directly on absence). One judgement, not a sibling copy that drifts (016b section 9).' This plan extends that helper and wires both lanes in the same commit, rather than adding a second renderer.

ROUND 2 — the prior-art search for the prune rule itself: `grep -rn 'prune_floor|floor_ratio|reconcil' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/` finds no floor/completeness guard of any shape (every 'reconcil' hit is reconcile_superseded_reviews — a review-status sweep with no delete — or comment prose). `grep -rn 'DELETE FROM' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/ services/` returns 15 statements; exactly four delete-what-this-run-did-not-see, none with a completeness check.

ROUND 2 — the new SQL PREPAREd and EXECUTEd against the live schema before submission (go build cannot parse SQL). All three statements plan and run; at the current commit every kind cohort reads confirmed==stored (func 3048/3048, method 1025/1025, struct 857/857, interface 33/33, alias 29/29) and paths 592/592, while the same statements against a bogus commit_sha return 0 confirmed of every cohort — i.e. the measurement correctly describes a total-loss run as 0%, which is what the floor refuses on. NOTE this corrects a figure carried in an older register entry: distinct paths are 592 today, not 530.

ROUND 2 — the image built from this commit carries the change: `strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c prune_floor_ratio` = 2 and `grep -c 'INDEX NOT AT ONE COMMIT'` = 1 in docker.io/aqls/agent-chassis:v1.0.1217, with a pre-existing positive control ('index_code_symbols: complete' = 1) in the same exec (bugs_open/153: a tag implies nothing).
code_symbols_actions.go, the prune as it stands: `DELETE FROM code_symbols WHERE repo = $1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2` — guarded by nothing but `if commitSHA != ""`.
bugs_open/135: 'Everything not re-upserted by THIS run is destroyed. That is correct when the run saw the whole repo, and catastrophic when it did not. Nothing checks that it did.'
bugs_open/135, on invisibility: 'A run that deleted 4,000 rows because it only saw 900 files reports pruned: 4000 and indexed: true. The number that should be the alarm is presented as output.'

bugs_open/135, bug_historian round 4 of corr 7ba5b8c4: 'This plan had the context and the call site open in front of it and chose to gate only the new addition, leaving the older, larger, already-populated half of the same table exposed to the identical mechanism.'

016b, generalisation of the confirm-the-fix pattern: 'Any confirm-the-fix path whose target can be deleted by something other than the fix: cache entries, rendered artefacts, generated files, child rows behind a DELETE+INSERT rebuild.' And the precedent it names: a full rebuild regenerating from plan_sections discarded a working interactive page — 'the interactive game is discarded, falling back to generic-text-block. Blast radius: one page (game-pathfinding)'.

diagnose_code_lookup_action.go, why the read side needs the note: the freshness read is `SELECT COALESCE(commit_sha,''), ... ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1`, i.e. ONE row, and its banner states 'it describes commit %s'.

diagnose_code_lookup_action.go on the read-side stakes: 'a stale index answers "absent" identically to a genuine absence, so at read time the answer must carry its own freshness — an empty result against a stale index is UNKNOWN, not evidence of absence, and nothing upstream can add that qualifier later.'

Live, measured 2026-07-31 via `SELECT repo, kind, commit_sha, count(*) FROM code_symbols GROUP BY 1,2,3`: one repo (gqls/agentchassis), 4,992 rows, five kinds (func 3048, method 1025, struct 857, interface 33, alias 29), ALL at commit d98010e8 — so every cohort ratio is ~1.0 today and arming the floor at 0.5 refuses nothing on a healthy run.

Live, measured 2026-07-31: `SELECT subject_type, subject_key, count(*) FROM doc_notes ...` returns action/index_code_symbols = 2 rows, confirming the trail this refusal joins rather than inventing a location. doc_notes.site_id is nullable; site_work_items.site_id/handler_agent/pipeline are NOT NULL (\d), which is why the latter cannot hold this.

The three unconverted call sites of the same shape, from `grep -rn 'DELETE FROM' --include=*.go`: populate_nav_tables_action.go:147 `DELETE FROM site_nav_items WHERE site_id = $1`, site_db_actions.go:1474 `DELETE FROM link_registry WHERE source_page_id = $1`, save_page_sections_action.go:532 `DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1 AND ...`.

The live code-indexer step config (agent_definitions, type='code-indexer', 2026-07-31) sets only commit_field / analysis_field / embedding_service — nothing sets prune_floor_ratio, so the guard arms at its code default.
plan.risks: ROUND 2 adds no code and therefore no new risk; the round-1 risk list stands unchanged below, with one item now PARTLY discharged: the SQL has been PREPAREd/EXECUTEd live and the built image pod-grepped, so 'not verified live' now means precisely one thing — the REFUSAL BRANCH has not yet been seen to fire in production, because the chassis has not been rolled (a roll would also have killed this council round mid-flight). The induction is scripted in the workstream RUNBOOK and is the gate on closing the case. ROUND 1 RISKS: 1. FALSE REFUSAL on a legitimate large deletion. A refactor that removes >50% of one kind's rows (interface has only 33 rows, alias 29, so a small kind is the realistic case) refuses the prune. Consequence is bounded and reversible: nothing is deleted, the stale rows are retained, and the remedy — lower or zero prune_floor_ratio for one run — is named in the refusal text itself. Reviewer should check that the remedy really is reachable from step config and that the refusal text says so. 2. RETAINED STALE ROWS become a part-stale index. Deliberate, and mitigated by the read-side note in the same commit; a reviewer should check whether any OTHER reader of code_symbols draws a freshness conclusion without going through codeIndexScope (lookup_code_symbols returns rows without a freshness claim; diagnose_route reads the index for scope resolution only). 3. The all-or-nothing refusal is a judgement call — per-kind selective pruning was considered and rejected as harder to reason about for a benefit the self-healing property mostly erases. Worth an objection if a reviewer disagrees. 4. TWO EXTRA QUERIES per indexing run (one GROUP BY over ~5k rows using idx_code_symbols_repo_kind, one count DISTINCT), on an action that already does thousands of upserts and embedding calls — negligible, but stated rather than assumed. 5. The doc_notes suppression window is hardcoded at 24h rather than config; deliberate (one more knob on a surface with no automated consumer), reviewable. 6. NOT verified live yet at submission time: the guard arms only when a chassis image ships. Planned induction, in the case file: insert synthetic rows under a bogus commit_sha so one kind's cohort falls below the floor, run the indexer, confirm the prune is REFUSED, the row count is unchanged, and the doc_note exists — then remove the synthetic rows and confirm a healthy run prunes normally. A green run over a healthy repo would only prove the guard is inert.
